section_headings: What are the genetics of OMFG?

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Chem D × Fog Dog; Runtz × Red Pop
Breeder: IC Collective / Exotic Genetix
THC Content: 20–30%
CBD Content: Typically very low
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , myrcene , linalool , humulene
Primary Flavors: Gas, tropical fruit, berry, cherry candy
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

OMFG is one of those cannabis names that requires more investigation than a quick glance at a dispensary label might suggest. Behind the provocative title are actually two established genetic versions: an IC Collective cultivar created from Chem D and Fog Dog, and a later Exotic Genetix release combining Runtz with Red Pop. The distinction is important because these are not minor phenotype variations of the same marijuana plant—they come from entirely different families.

IC Collective’s version is dominated by Chem-style fuel, fruit, funk, and exceptional potency, while Exotic Genetix takes OMFG toward cherry candy, berries, citrus, and the sugary terpene territory of modern Runtz breeding. Both can produce powerful weed with strong resin coverage, but they should not be treated as genetically interchangeable. For strain-library purposes, understanding this naming overlap gives a far more accurate picture than assigning OMFG a single pedigree without identifying the breeder.
Genetics and Lineage

The earlier documented OMFG comes from IC Collective, which identifies its cultivar as Chem D × Fog Dog. According to the breeder, Fog Dog pollen unexpectedly reached a Chem D female and produced several promising offspring. OMFG emerged from that event and was introduced to the California market in 2018 before later becoming part of IC Collective’s Illinois catalog. Chem D contributes the intensely pungent fuel character for which the Chem family is famous—an aroma the breeder compares with gasoline and fresh tennis balls—while Fog Dog adds tighter flower structure and a distinctly fruity, funky character. IC Collective describes OMFG as one of its original genetics rather than an outside cultivar adopted under the company name.

Exotic Genetix subsequently released a completely different OMFG made by crossing Runtz with Red Pop. A current breeder-verified retail listing confirms Runtz × Red Pop and identifies the cultivar as a feminized photoperiod hybrid with approximately nine weeks of flowering. Runtz introduces its famous Zkittlez and Gelato derived candy profile, while Red Pop brings berry soda, strawberry sweetness, and Cookies & Cream ancestry. The Red Pop selection itself originated from a Strawberries and Cream phenotype valued for an aroma reminiscent of bright red strawberry soda. Together, the parents move this version of OMFG away from old-school Chem funk and toward a much sweeter candy-and-fruit expression.
Effects and Experience

Whichever version is encountered, OMFG generally belongs in the high-potency end of the cannabis spectrum, although the experience differs somewhat according to genetics. IC Collective’s Chem D × Fog Dog cut has a reputation for hitting hard. The breeder reports average total THC around 30% and average terpene content around 3.62%, describing the effect as a combination of pronounced body relaxation and an intense euphoric head high. The onset can feel forceful and mentally expansive, followed by a heavier physical sensation that makes the cultivar more appropriate for experienced consumers than someone testing strong marijuana for the first time.

Exotic Genetix’s Runtz × Red Pop version tends to present a somewhat softer balance between mental enjoyment and physical relaxation. Seed-stock information places THC around 20–24% and characterizes the effects as relaxed, creative, and balanced. Mood elevation can emerge early, with music, conversation, hobbies, or entertainment becoming more absorbing before a comfortable body calm settles in. Even at the lower end of OMFG potency, however, this is not lightweight weed. Larger doses can interfere with concentration and coordination, and consumers sensitive to THC may experience dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, or an uncomfortable degree of mental intensity.
Medical Benefits

The combination of euphoria and body relaxation may explain why OMFG attracts some medical marijuana consumers seeking temporary relief from stress, physical tension, low mood, or difficulty settling down. The Chem D × Fog Dog version is particularly body-oriented after its initial cerebral surge, whereas the Runtz × Red Pop cultivar may provide a more gradual transition from upbeat mental effects into relaxation. Either profile could appeal to consumers who want strong evening cannabis without selecting a strain solely for immediate sedation.

A strain name, however, does not establish medical effectiveness. That warning is especially relevant here because OMFG can refer to two genetically unrelated cultivars with very different cannabinoid and terpene profiles. A product containing close to 30% THC may behave very differently from another carrying the same name at 20–22%. Anyone using marijuana therapeutically should therefore evaluate the specific product’s laboratory analysis, dose, delivery method, personal THC sensitivity, and interactions with medications rather than assuming every OMFG product will produce the same result.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The IC Collective phenotype is the choice for consumers who prefer cannabis with a classic Chem foundation. Its aroma begins with gasoline, rubbery funk, and an almost industrial sharpness before Fog Dog introduces ripe fruit and a sweeter, rank quality. The breeder characterizes the combination as funky and spicy with fresh fruity high notes layered over the Chem D base. This contrast is central to the cultivar’s identity: the fruit does not erase the fuel, and the gas keeps the sweeter elements from resembling a conventional dessert strain.

Exotic Genetix’s release inhabits a very different aromatic neighborhood. Runtz × Red Pop material is commonly described through grapefruit, cherry, candy, and gas, with caryophyllene, linalool, and humulene listed among its important terpenes. Cherry and berry soda are particularly logical expressions of the Red Pop parent, while Runtz contributes tropical candy and creamy fruit. Caryophyllene reinforces pepper and spice, humulene can add dry herbal depth, and linalool introduces a softer floral quality. The inhale tends toward fruit candy and citrus, while the finish can become earthier, spicier, and slightly gassy.
Growing Information

Cultivation information is considerably clearer for the Exotic Genetix version because it was released as feminized seed. Breeder-linked listings place its flowering period at approximately 56–63 days, or eight to nine weeks, with medium to medium-tall growth. One verified partner classifies it simply as an indica/sativa mix and confirms that it can be cultivated indoors, in greenhouses, or outdoors. Other release information describes the plants as roughly 60–70% indica-leaning, demonstrating that numerical indica/sativa percentages should be treated as approximate rather than botanical measurements.

A multi-topped canopy suits the Exotic Genetix cultivar well. Topping during vegetative growth can create several productive branches instead of one dominant central cola, while low-stress training helps distribute those branches across available light. An eight-to-nine-week flowering period generally points toward an early-October outdoor finish in favorable Northern Hemisphere environments. Yield is usually characterized as moderate rather than exceptional, though healthy plants with sufficient light, root space, and canopy management can outperform generalized seed-catalog estimates.

The IC Collective cut is more commonly encountered as proprietary commercial genetics than as broadly distributed seed stock. IC Collective emphasizes its tight flower structure, potency, and terpene expression rather than publishing a standardized home-growing schedule. Its dense buds and substantial resin production make late-flower airflow particularly important. With either cultivar, growers should confirm the genetic source before applying strain-specific cultivation advice; recommendations intended for Runtz × Red Pop cannot automatically be assumed to apply to Chem D × Fog Dog.
FAQ
What are the genetics of OMFG?

There are two well-documented OMFG cannabis strains. IC Collective’s original cultivar is Chem D × Fog Dog and was introduced in California in 2018. Exotic Genetix later released a separate OMFG from Runtz × Red Pop.
Who bred the OMFG strain?

IC Collective bred the Chem D × Fog Dog version, while Exotic Genetix bred the Runtz × Red Pop version. Because the genetics are completely different, identifying the breeder is essential when purchasing OMFG flower, seeds, or clones.
Is OMFG indica or sativa?

OMFG is generally treated as a hybrid. The Exotic Genetix version leans indica in several commercial descriptions, while the IC Collective cultivar combines a strong cerebral high with substantial body relaxation. Neither should be judged solely by an indica/sativa percentage.
How strong is OMFG?

Potency depends heavily on which cultivar is involved. IC Collective reports its Chem D × Fog Dog selection at approximately 30% average total THC, while Exotic Genetix seed-stock descriptions generally place Runtz × Red Pop around 20–24% THC. Individual harvests can fall outside either range.
What does OMFG taste like?

The IC Collective cultivar emphasizes gasoline, Chem funk, fruit, and spice. Exotic Genetix’s version is considerably sweeter, combining cherry, grapefruit, berry candy, and gas. Checking the breeder tells consumers much more about the expected flavor than the OMFG name alone.
Final Thoughts on OMFG

OMFG demonstrates one of the biggest challenges involved in documenting modern marijuana strains : names are not standardized genetic identifiers. IC Collective’s Chem D × Fog Dog cultivar and Exotic Genetix’s Runtz × Red Pop hybrid share a name but virtually nothing else in their immediate ancestry. The former traces its personality to Chem-style gasoline, intense potency, fruit, and funk, while the latter represents the modern candy movement through Runtz and the strawberry-soda qualities of Red Pop.

Both versions have reasons to command attention. IC Collective reports exceptional THC and terpene concentrations from a cultivar it has preserved since its California days, while Exotic Genetix offers a relatively fast eight-to-nine-week feminized strain with accessible growth characteristics and a distinctly sweeter flavor profile. For anyone researching, growing, or buying OMFG, the most important question is therefore not simply whether the strain is good—it is which OMFG is actually in the jar. Identifying the breeder turns an ambiguous name into a meaningful description of the genetics, flavor, potency, and overall cannabis experience.
